gaps.lead: 'Did you send the invoice?' the manager asked her.
gaps.explanation: if/whether + subject + backshifted verb: whether she had sent.

gaps.lead: Brian was really interested in North American history in his school days.
gaps.sentence: Brian ___ North American history in his school days.
gaps.hint: be interested in = have an ___ in
gaps.explanation: 'To be interested in' becomes the noun pattern: 'had an interest in'.

gaps.lead: I want you to stop tapping your pen while I am working.
gaps.sentence: I ___ tapping your pen while I am working.
gaps.explanation: 'I want you to stop' becomes 'I wish you would stop' — wish + would for irritation.

gaps.lead: My grandfather planted all these apple trees himself.
gaps.sentence: My grandfather is the ___ all these apple trees.
gaps.explanation: 'the one who…' identifies the agent with a relative clause.

gaps.lead: Somebody is repairing our roof at the moment.
gaps.explanation: Somebody else is doing it for us: we are having our roof repaired.

gaps.lead: Barbara's parents were certain that she would be a great tennis player.
gaps.sentence: Barbara's parents were ___ that she would be a great tennis player.

gaps.lead: Yesterday, I informed my boss in writing that I would be leaving the company.
gaps.hint: inform your employer in writing = hand in your ___
gaps.explanation: 'Hand in one's notice' means formally resign.

gaps.lead: I'm sure we went the wrong way at the last junction.
gaps.hint: must have + participle for past deduction
gaps.explanation: A deduction about the past: 'must have taken'.
